statement: A snail crawls 3 millimetres every second. Moving at this steady speed, how many metres does it travel in one hour?

choices.misconception: I multiplied by 60 only, which turns seconds into minutes, so I found the distance for one minute.
I used 360 seconds in an hour instead of 3600.
I divided 10800 millimetres by 100, thinking a metre is 100 millimetres.
I found the distance in millimetres and forgot to change it into metres.

hints: Find the distance in millimetres first, then convert.
An hour is 60 minutes of 60 seconds each. Multiply to get the millimetres travelled in an hour, then remember how many millimetres make one metre.
3 x 3600 = 10800 millimetres, and a metre is 1000 millimetres.

solutions.reliable: One hour is 60 x 60 = 3600 seconds, so the snail crawls 3 x 3600 = 10800 millimetres. A metre is 1000 millimetres, so that is 10800 / 1000 = 10.8 metres. The transferable idea: convert in small named steps and write the unit at every step, because each slip changes the answer by a power of ten.

whyOnTest: Unit conversion questions check that time and length are converted with the right factors, and every slip gives one of the choices.
